CHEAP_DATA_NOW: SEC TYG/MPTI offering documents explicitly list exchange-traded transferable rights and expiry/last-trading dates. General Yahoo stock OHLC schema exists, but this expired temporary instrument alias is unverified and returned 404. No free right bid/ask or exercise-fill route qualified.
CHEAP_EXPRESSION: Buy a fixed basic entitlement, pay exercise cash, exit common shares at a frozen session after issuance; account for all right costs, exercise deadline and dilution. Do not claim oversubscription eligibility for a new buyer.
ECONOMIC_SIGNIFICANCE: Post-record-date basic exercise is documented, but no measurable forced-selling rent.
FATAL_PROBLEM: Complete temporary-symbol price mapping, spreads and delivery clock missing. Subscription discount alone ignores rights cost. This is related rights-funding exposure, not an independent family reset or reopening the parked record-holder oversubscription expression.
LESSON: Do not confuse transferable basic rights with record-holder-only residual privileges; last trading day is not the broker exercise cutoff.
MECHANISM: Record holders unable or unwilling to exercise transferable subscription rights may sell a short-lived entitlement under deadline pressure; a new small buyer can potentially exercise basic rights without record-date ownership.
NEXT_DECISION: Only reopen with a concrete temporary-symbol mapping and free quote/delivery facts. Next L0 FDA recall disclosure diffusion; check public-time semantics.
POWER_LIMITATION: No matched right/common price or payoff.
UNCERTAINTY: A 404 on an unverified expired alias is not proof no free rights history exists.
WHO_PAYS: Nonparticipating right holders demanding liquidity and existing holders diluted by issuance; any rent must survive both right purchase cost and common-share/dilution risk.
WHY_PERSIST: Temporary symbols, broker exercise cutoffs, tiny lots, capital calls and irreversible expiry create operational nuisance; institutions can still price the rights and are not categorically excluded.
